subject: Recap & next steps: model fit, safety eval plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@carewell.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@carewell.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps: model fit, safety eval plan

Hi Ellen / Rajiv —

Thanks for the call today — quick recap and suggested next steps so we all have the same plan: 

Key takeaways (from your side)
- Primary use: clinical intake triage + templated care-plan suggestions (no diagnoses).
- Safety/regulatory constraints: must refuse when asked for PHI extraction or explicit diagnosis; require strong, auditable refusal behavior and user-facing safe fallbacks.
- Performance targets: p95 latency < 300ms for short responses (<128 tokens) at pilot throughput ~10 qps.
- Success criteria: accuracy on structured extraction testset (F1 > 0.78), refusal rate on sensitive prompts > 95% where appropriate, and low hallucination rate on factual prompts.

Recommended evaluation approach (what we'll run for the pilot)
1) Model shortlist to trial (provision 7-day eval nodes):
   - redwood/virtus-7b-q5 (low-cost, strong refusal baseline)
   - redwood/consent-13b (better instruction-following, stronger guardrail primitives)
   - open/mixtral-8x7b (external comparator for hallucination/throughput)
2) Benchmarks: we will run the CareWell sample prompt set + your tagged edge-cases. See summary PDF attached and the live benchmark run link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/main/carewell-2027
3) Safety/refusal eval: dynamic prompt set with ~350 sensitive scenarios (PHI, medical advice, PII leakage) to measure false negatives/positives and to tune refusal prompts.
4) Metrics & artifacts we will deliver: refusal logs, per-prompt model outputs, token cost estimates, p95 latency traces, and recommended fallback prompts.

Attachments included: carewell_sample_prompts_v1.json (prompt set we used on the call), model_benchmarks_summary_202702.pdf (high-level expected perf/cost ranges).

Immediate next steps
- You: share a representative anonymized sample of 200 intake transcripts by EOD Wed (if possible).
- Us: provision the three eval nodes and run an initial smoke test (target by Wed EOD).
- Schedule: propose Wed 10 Feb 11:00 AM PT for a kickoff/observability walkthrough.
- Procurement: flagging that if you want dedicated/pinned capacity for production we'll need Procurement contact and contract timeline (we can run pilot on hosted eval without contract).

Questions for you
- Any specific refusal wording/legal phrasing CareWell needs us to use as the user-facing message?
- Are there internal reviewers (privacy/security) we should include on the SOC2/DPA conversation?

Thanks again — I’ll t-shirt the eval plan with Neha and Sergio and loop Camila on benchmarks.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear plan, this aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick items from our compliance/legal side: 

- SOC2 report and the DPA are required before we can move any production data into a hosted environment. Can you share current SOC2 attestations and your standard DPA?
- For the refusal messages, our legal team wants the default phrasing to avoid clinical language (we prefer: "I can’t help with that request. Please consult a qualified clinician."). Are you able to force that phrasing as part of the refusal-response pipeline?
- On the safety eval: will you provide per-prompt logs showing when the model refused vs. replied? We need that for audit.

If you can send the SOC2 + DPA and confirm the refusal phrasing and logs, we can get the sample transcripts to you by Wed. Also cc'd Rajiv (engineering) — he may ask about latency/embedding config later.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Product, CareWell Health
ellen.park@carewell.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@carewell.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@carewell.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: model fit, safety eval plan

Ellen / Rajiv —

Quick answers: yes to all, and here’s how we will handle each ask.

SOC2 / DPA
- I’ve attached the latest SOC2 Type II summary in the secure Drive link (full attestation will be shared via our legal portal). Our standard DPA is provided as a DocuSign link — if you want, I can route it to your procurement contact for signature.

Refusal phrasing + audit logs
- We can enforce the exact refusal phrase you specified as a last-line guardrail in the response pipeline. Implementation options: server-side rewrite of model output OR prompt-level hard-stop + canonical refusal template. We recommend prompt-level guardrail + post-output validation to ensure auditability.
- We will deliver per-prompt logs for the safety eval: input prompt, model raw output, final served output (after canonicalization), decision flag (refused/served), timestamp, and model id. These will be available in the Console export CSV and as a zipped artifact for the pilot.

Safety eval mechanics (we will run)
- Run 3 model variants against the 350-case sensitive prompt set + 200 care intake transcripts you provide.
- Metrics: refusal precision/recall, false negatives where model provided disallowed content, and per-case latency.
- Deliverables: refusal-rate matrix, sample failing prompts, recommended guardrail prompts for production, and a short remediation plan for any model that underperforms.

Operational asks for Redwood team
- Neha: please provision 3 eval nodes (virtus-7b, consent-13b, mixtral-8x7b) with logging enabled and prefix KV caching off for the first run; schedule smoke tests Wed morning.
- Sergio: can you pull the SOC2 summary and DPA doc and share the Legal/Procurement link with Ellen?

Ellen — if you confirm the kickoff time (Wed 10 Feb 11:00 AM PT) I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda: smoke test demo, Console walkthrough for logs, and timeline for deliverables.

Thanks,
Jordan
